Automated update to Github CI workflow `cont_integration.yml` by [create-pull-request](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request) GitHub action

I manually fixed new clippy warnings.

I also changed CI to:
~~1. not build or run tests or test dependencies when building with MSRV.  This reduced the number of dependencies we need to pin for MSRV and fixes 1398.~~ I removed these changes.
2. use the same version or rust as in the `rust-version` file for all jobs instead of just for clippy. I made this change to prevent CI breaks when stable changes before we have a chance to fix the auto created PR that bumps the `rust-version` file.

body:
<!-- PR Title format: "<JIRA_TICKET_ID>: <TICKET_TITLE>"-->

## Issue
https://raquelanaroman.atlassian.net/browse/HER-29

As a user I would like to be able to view my profile page.

The JSON response from the backend should be:
{
   "id": ,
    "name": ,
    "email": ,
    "donations": [
    {
    "amount": ,
    "created_at": ,
    }
  ],
"orders": [
    {
    "requested_kit": ,
    "address": ,
    "school_year": ,
    "phone": ,
    "comments": , 
    }
  ],
}

Acceptance Criteria: 
- Create a user profile interface 
   - Retrieve data from /api/v1/users/profile
   - Render the elements of the profile
   - Handle missing information from API response
   - Link users to:
     - make donation
     - order kits
     - request speakers

Links: 
-https://raquelanaroman.atlassian.net/browse/HER-30
-https://raquelanaroman.atlassian.net/browse/HER-28

## Changes
- Added `UserProfile` component in React.js
- Fetched user data with `fetch` in `useEffect`
- Rendered donations and orders with fallback messages
- Linked to "Make Donation," "Order Kits," and "Request Speakers"

### Review Checklist

- [ ] I have documented my code with code comments.

## Summary
This PR uses [Goreleaser](https://goreleaser.com) to publish binaries, linux packages, and homebrew formula manifests for the Datum Cloud CLI. 

- Release artifacts are published to the GitHub Release
  - Software Binaries
  - SBOM
  - Linux packages
    - apk
    - deb
    - rpm
    - termux.deb
    - archlinux
- Homebrew forumula manifest is pushed to [datum-cloud/homebrew-tap](https://github.com/datum-cloud/homebrew-tap)

## Installing via Homebrew

This example was based on an example release that was published.

```shell
$ brew tap datum-cloud/tap
==> Tapping datum-cloud/tap
Cloning into '/opt/homebrew/Library/Taps/datum-cloud/homebrew-tap'...
...

$ brew install datum-cloud/tap/cli
==> Fetching datum-cloud/tap/cli
==> Downloading https://github.com/datum-cloud/datumctl/releases/download/v0.0.1-rc9/datumctl_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
...

$ datumctl --help
A CLI for Datum Cloud

Usage:
  datumctl [command]

Available Commands:
  auth        Authenticate with Datum Cloud
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for datumctl

Use "datumctl [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

author: loterence
body:
Fixes #622

Lazy loading react components (code splitting) now works in production.

This issue was caused by django templates not able to load the static js file needed to render the qualifiers page.

### Changes

- remove `django-vite` integration
- redo stage build so that it doesn't use django templates in the backend
- moved `index.html` template file into frontend folder, so its 100% handled by vite
- split the frontend and backend development servers in dev mode.
    - now we have to access the backend with `localhost:8000` and the frontend with `localhost:5175` in dev mode.
    - frontend static files are still served from django backend in prod mode
    - I had to do this instead of proxying because frontend `.svg?react` and `svg?url` content-type headers doesn't allow for proxying
- adjusted docker config

author: krispymb
body:
Arguably as a bug, Clang has previously not mixed up Objective-C parameter names with types. This allows developers to write parameter names that _should_ shadow type names, but don't. For instance:

    @interface Foo
    -(void)foo:(int)id bar:(id)name; // OK
    @end

Commit 97788089988a2ace63d717cadbcfe3443f380f9c changed the way that parameters are parsed to bring it more in line with how C parameters are parsed, but it breaks the example above. Given an expectation that the change wouldn't introduce source breaks, this is not something we can go forward with.

977880... did this so that late-parsed attributes could reference Objective-C parameters. This change buffers Objective-C parameter info until after all parameters are parsed and turns them into parameter declarations before realizing late-parsed attributes instead.

Radar-ID: 139996306
(cherry picked from commit d8c7c55237019791ec3badea535ca227bd22845a)

body:
# Changelog

## Break Handler
- **Added**: Option to only allow micro breaks via Antiban this will prevent the plugin from taking longer breaks and logging out.

## Mahogany Homes Plugin
- **Added**: Support for NPC Contact spell to get new contracts.
- **Fixed**: Contract dialogues now correctly handle the "Continue" option before selecting a contract.
- **Changed**: Banking will now be done at the closest bank to the contract location instead of the closest bank to the player.

## QoL Plugin
- **Fixed**: NeverLogOut now correctly handles the logout timer.
- **Changed**: Extracted and refactored some of the code to make it more modular.
- **Added**: Auto-Drop option in "Inventory/Equipment" tab to drop items when inventory is full.

## Motherlode Mine Plugin
- **Fixed**: Nolonger gets stuck in idle state if user interrupts the plugin.
- **Added**: Check in settings if upstairs hopper is unlocked. If not, it will use the downstairs hopper while still mining upstairs.
- - **Updated**: Replaced a deprecated method in the API.

## Amethyst Mine Plugin
- **Fixed**: Nolonger gets stuck in idle state if user interrupts the plugin.
- **Added**: support for gem bag.

## Tempoross Plugin
- **Added**: Antiban support.

## AIO Fighter Plugin
- **Added**: Loot List option to select what items to loot.

## Varrock Anvil Plugin
- **Adjusted** Increased the timeout timer from 5 seconds to 10 seconds when waiting for the anvil interface to open to prevent the plugin from getting stuck if player doesn't have run energy.

## Rs2Player Class
- **Fixed**: ``checkIdleLogout`` now does correct calculations.

## Natural Mouse
- **Fixed** Scroll Up now works properly.

## Rs2Antiban Class
- **Updated**: Replaced a deprecated method in the API.

## Rs2Bank Class
- **Added**: Method to empty gem bag.
- **Added**: Method ``getNearestBank(WorldPoint worldPoint)`` to get the nearest bank to a given world point.

## Global Class
- **Added**: Method ``sleepUntil`` with a runnable action while waiting.

## Rs2UiHelper Class
- **Added**: Helper method ``isRectangleWithinRectangle`` to check if a rectangle is within another rectangle.

## Rs2Magic Class
- **Fixed**: Method ``npcContact`` will now check if npc widget is visible before interacting with it if not visible it will scroll to it.
- **Updated**: Replaced a deprecated method in the API.

author: wilfranr
body:
1. Validación y normalización del campo tipo:
Primera letra en mayúscula: Inicialmente, configuramos el campo tipo para que su primera letra fuera en mayúscula utilizando ucfirst().
Valores específicos permitidos: Añadimos una validación para asegurarnos de que el valor de tipo estuviera dentro de una lista predefinida de valores permitidos ($allowedTipos).
Conversión a mayúsculas: Simplificamos el código para que todos los valores de tipo se conviertan a mayúsculas con mb_strtoupper(), garantizando consistencia en el formato.
2. Botón para descargar un archivo Excel:
Creamos una ruta en Laravel para que el botón permita descargar un archivo de Excel ubicado en la carpeta public/plantillas/.
Actualizamos el componente <x-filament::button> para que apunte a la ruta creada, utilizando href="{{ route('descargar-plantilla') }}".
3. Estilización del botón:
Ajustamos el botón para hacerlo más pequeño agregando clases de Tailwind CSS (px-2 py-1 text-sm) y personalizamos su diseño.
También propusimos estilos adicionales para darle un color de fondo, un color de texto, y efectos al pasar el mouse (hover).
Resultado Final:
Se creó una validación robusta para el campo tipo en el modelo, asegurando que los valores sean consistentes y permitidos.
Se implementó un botón funcional y estilizado para descargar plantillas de Excel.
El diseño del botón fue ajustado para adaptarse a tus preferencias visuales.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change replaces the usage of [`java.io.File#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/io/File.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)) with [`java.nio.file.Files#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/file/Files.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute...)) which has more secure attributes.

The `java.io.File#createTempFile()` method creates a file that is world-readable and world-writeable, which is almost never necessary. Also, the file created is placed in a predictable directory (e.g., `/tmp`). Having predictable file names, locations, and will lead to many types of vulnerabilities. History has shown that this insecure pattern can lead to [information leakage](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-28168/), [privilege escalation](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-29428/) and even [code execution](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2022/02/25/3).

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
+  import java.nio.file.Files;
   ...
-  File txtFile = File.createTempFile("acme", ".txt");
+  File txtFile = Files.createTempFile("acme", ".txt").toFile();
```

### **PR Type** Enhancement ___ ### **Description** This PR integrates LiteLLM for zero-shot chat completions. It introduces a new `LiteLLMClient` that interacts with the LiteLLM API using `RestClient`. The client is configured with properties from `LiteLLMProperties`. Request and response payloads are defined, and unit tests are implemented using `MockRestServiceServer`. Additionally, necessary dependencies are added to the project. ___ ### **Changes walkthrough** 📝

Enhancement
LiteLLMClient.java
Implement LiteLLMClient for Zero-Shot Chat Completions     
backend/src/main/java/com/aqryuz/backend/litellm/client/LiteLLMClient.java
  • A new LiteLLMClient is introduced, which interacts with a LiteLLM
    service.
  • The client uses RestClient to make requests to the LiteLLM API.
  • A zeroShot method is implemented, enabling zero-shot chat completions.
  • The client is configured with a base URL and API key from
    LiteLLMProperties.
    		•  +37/-0   
    ChatCompletionsRequest.java
    Define Chat Completion Request Payload Structure                 
    backend/src/main/java/com/aqryuz/backend/litellm/client/payload/ChatCompletionsRequest.java
  • Defines the request payload structure for chat completions.
  • Includes fields for model, messages, temperature, max tokens, top_p,
    frequency penalty, presence penalty, and stop sequences.
  • Provides a constructor with default values for the model.
  • Defines an inner record ChatMessage for representing individual
    messages with role and content.

    Define Chat Completion Response Payload Structure

  • Defines the response payload structure for chat completions.
  • Includes fields for id, choices, creation timestamp, model, and usage
    statistics.
  • Defines inner records for AIChoice, AIMessage, and AIUsage to
    represent the nested structure of the response.
    		•  +21/-0   
    Configuration changes
    LiteLLMProperties.java
    Define LiteLLM API Configuration Properties

  • Defines a configuration class LiteLLMProperties to store LiteLLM API

author: feasel0
body:
Fixes errors that were causing `libSupportTests` (`lib/support/tests`) unit tests to fail on ESP32.
- [Log before changes](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18847421/libSupportTests.1.txt) (9 failures)
- [Log after changes](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18847805/libSupportTests-after.txt) (0 failures)

Changes

- Adds the unit tests `src/lib/support/tests` into the `esp32-qemu-tests` target.
- Updates `ArgParser::ParseArgs()` to work with platforms with a non-POSIX `getopt_long` (like ESP32).  This was causing failures in some of the test cases in `TestCHIPArgParser.cpp`.
- Updates `EncodeTlvElement()` to work with platforms where `malloc(0)` returns null (like ESP32).  This was causing a failure when building zero-length strings, since the null response was being interpreted as "out of memory".
- Updates `.vscode/tasks.json` to include Build and Run tasks for the ESP32 unit tests.
- Adds a `clean.sh` script for removing the files generated by the ESP32 unit test build.

How is ESP32's `getopt_long` different from the POSIX version?

- Sets optopt to '?' when encountering an unknown short option, instead of setting it to the actual value of the character it encountered.
- Treats an unknown long option like a series of short options.
- Does not always permute argv to put the nonoptions at the end.

As a result, ParseArgs needs to do a little more work when interpreting the results of `getopt_long`.  This code is only executed if `CONFIG_NON_POSIX_GETOPT_LONG` is defined, which happens automatically in `src/lib/support/BUILD.gn` when `chip_device_platform` is "esp32".

#### Testing

Automated testing.  Used the `ESP32_QEMU` CI check, which now includes `libSupportTests`.  Also manually built the `esp32-qemu-tests` target and ran all images.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
Many developers will be surprised to learn that `requests` library calls do not include timeouts by default. This means that an attempted request could hang indefinitely if no connection is established or if no data is received from the server. 

The [requests documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts) suggests that most calls should explicitly include a `timeout` parameter. This codemod adds a default timeout value in order to set an upper bound on connection times and ensure that requests connect or fail in a timely manner. This value also ensures the connection will timeout if the server does not respond with data within a reasonable amount of time. 

While timeout values will be application dependent, we believe that this codemod adds a reasonable default that serves as an appropriate ceiling for most situations. 

Our changes look like the following:
```diff
 import requests
 
- requests.get("http://example.com")
+ requests.get("http://example.com", timeout=60)
```

<details>
  <summary>More reading</summary>

  * [https://docs.python-requests.org/en/master/user/quickstart/#timeouts](https://docs.python-requests.org/en/master/user/quickstart/#timeouts)

author: ynojima
body:
Follow-up for #44105 and #45132. ~~#45132 need to be merged first.~~(#45132 was already merged)

- Renames the endpoints from `register-options-challenge`  and `login-options-challenge` to `register-options` and `login-options`
- Update security-webauthn.doc to clarify that WebAuthn uses a challenge-response machanism to protect from replay attacks, and that the challenge can be obtained by calling the options endpoint

I am sorry for repeatedly bringing this up, but since the endpoints now are `GET` method and behaves idempotently and don't have a big side-effect for challenge, it is good chance to rename them to `register-options` and `login-options`.

body:
**Team Members**
---
| Name | Student ID | Contribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pham Tran Gia Phu | 2352921 | Implemented Genetic Algorithm |
| Vo Hoang Anh Kiet | 2352659 | Implemented Genetic Algorithm |
| Nguyen Tran Trong Tuyen | 2353283 | Implemented First-Fit Decreasing Algorithm |
| Nguyen Huu Cau | 2352129 | Problem Formulation |
| Bui Huy Phuong | 2352948 | Theories & Case Studies |

**Brief Description**
---
This submission introduces two policy implementations for the cutting stock problem:
- **Genetic algorithm**: The Genetic algorithm in the document is designed to solve the two-dimensional rectangular cutting stock problem (2DRSSSCSP) with the objective of balancing material utilization and cutting complexity. It uses a combination of two-staged patterns (2SGP) and three-staged patterns (3SHP) to create an efficient cutting plan.
- **First-Fit Decreasing algorithm**: he First Fit algorithm is an optimization problem solving strategy, where decisions are made based on the best local criteria at each step, aiming to achieve a globally optimal solution. Instead of considering all possibilities, the algorithm focuses only on the best choice at the moment.

**Summarized Results**
---
| Criteria | First-Fit Decreasing | Genetic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Algorithm complexity | Low | Moderate to high |
| Material utilization eficiency | Not globally optimal | More optimized, less waste |
| Computation time | Short | Longer due to complexity |
| Apllication | Simple problems | Complex and diverse problems |

author: susumutomita
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the `saba_core` module, including the addition of a new `Browser` struct, enhancements to the `Page` struct, and the addition of utility functions for DOM manipulation. It also includes a minor update to the `docker-compose.yml` file to support ARM64 architecture. The most important changes are summarized below:

### Browser and Page Implementation:

* [`saba_core/src/browser.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-a0497ffc20117788a11e750045303e2f0e7ec5dfe96fd804c7e36fdafb9f8bd2R1-R27): Added a new `Browser` struct with methods to manage pages and retrieve the current page.
* [`saba_core/src/renderer/page.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-35388c742a0b9dbbaf5e9b7ca4f609d326c451e1984d5b8cc8cf2a8113070f1eR1-R58): Introduced a `Page` struct with methods to set the browser, set the frame, receive HTTP responses, and convert DOM to string.

### Module and Utility Additions:

* [`saba_core/src/lib.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-a7b2c291dc420c0fa75a606e057c83a36ad3150a165f63a24ae888624364d783R5-R10): Added `browser` and `utils` modules to the `saba_core` library.
* [`saba_core/src/renderer/mod.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-9dbc791d2ceee182f5fa2adb777ab50f69b285123f841e324696daf3851a55feR3): Added the `page` module to the renderer.
* [`saba_core/src/utils.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-cd86142285d0290ccfa133df50c2cc8599dd8cc15bcd26d939b0f17da3595dc9R1-R29): Implemented utility functions for converting DOM nodes to strings.

### Main Application Update:

* [`src/main.rs`](diffhunk://#diff-42cb6807ad74b3e201c5a7ca98b911c5fa08380e942be6e4ac5807f8377f87fcL6-R33): Updated the main application to use the new `Browser` and `HttpResponse` classes, and included a static test HTTP response.

### Docker Configuration:

* [`docker-compose.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3R4): Added support for ARM64 architecture in the `browser-dev` service.

    v7.26.0 (2024-10-25)

author: ferdnyc
body:
This PR started as an effort to reduce repetition in our project extras, and kind of exploded from there — not always in especially useful ways. But it does achieve two practical benefits:

1. The aforementioned decrease in redundancy. Now, instead of the `tests` extra containing all of the same packages as the `dev` extra, it just contains `pydot[dev]`. (Because, turns out you can do that!)
2. A newly-added `types` extra, containing only `mypy`, is used in the `mypy-check` tox environment, avoiding the installation of all of the other packages in `pydot[dev]` that aren't needed for mypy checking.

Both the `dev` and `tests` extras contain the exact same set of packages before and after this PR, to avoid messing with anyone's habits/expectations. This PR just arranges to achieve that in a non-redundant manner.

author: shellysela219
body:
fix for "when VPD length is aligned on a 4B boundary, mstvpd fails due "-E- Failed to parse VPD from 21:00.0!"

Description: mvpd_len was not calculated correctly: It always missed the 1-byte length of the end tag. this was masked by the fact that mvpd_get_raw_vpd() calls my_vpd_read() and always reads 4 bytes at a time, so when the vpd len is not aligned on a 4B boundary, the 4B read covered the extra byte needed with the end tag len since it is only 1 byte. but when the vpd len is aligned on a 4B boundary, mvpd_len is calculated by reading all the VPD, yet not the end tag, which causes this error: "-E- Failed to parse VPD from 21:00.0!"

Tested OS: linux
Tested devices: n/a
Tested flows: mstvpd 21:00.0

Known gaps (with RM ticket): n/a

Issue: 4209502

author: nguyenthinhthanh
body:
# Group member - Nguyễn Thịnh Thành 2213140 - Nguyễn Trường Giang 2210830 - Nguyễn Thiên Trí 2313612 - Vương Minh Khôi 2311712 - Tô Thế Hưng 2211384 # Policy Descriptions ## 1. First-Fit Decreasing Heuristic First-Fit Decreasing Heurizstic (FFD) là một thuật toán heuristic phổ biến để giải quyết bài toán cutting stock và các bài toán đóng gói (packing problem). Thuật toán FFD đặc biệt hiệu quả trong các bài toán 2D cutting stock, nơi cần tối ưu hóa cách cắt các hình chữ nhật từ vật liệu để giảm thiểu lãng phí. FFD được xây dựng trên hai bước chính: - Sắp xếp giảm dần (Decreasing order): - First-Fit (Lựa chọn khớp đầu tiên): FFD tận dụng ý tưởng ưu tiên các stock lớn trước và đặt hình vào các tấm sẵn có để giảm số lượng tấm cần sử dụng. Điều này giúp: - Tối ưu hóa không gian: Các hình lớn được xử lý trước, tránh tình trạng các hình lớn không thể được đặt vào các không gian nhỏ còn lại. - Tăng tốc độ tính toán: Thuật toán heuristic có độ phức tạp thấp hơn so với các thuật toán tối ưu chính xác (như quy hoạch nguyên). ## 2. Best Fit Decrease Heuristic Thuật toán Best Fit Decrease (BFD) là một biến thể của thuật toán Best Fit, được sử dụng để giải quyết bài toán cắt vật liệu 2 chiều. Phương pháp này có thể được mô tả qua các bước sau: - Sắp xếp các vật phẩm cần cắt theo chiều giảm dần của diện tích (hoặc chiều dài và chiều rộng) trước khi thực hiện cắt. Việc này giúp xử lý các vật phẩm lớn trước, tối ưu hóa diện tích của tấm vật liệu lớn hơn. - Duyệt qua từng vật phẩm: Tìm các tấm vật liệu đã cắt (thường là một tấm lớn đã được cắt thành nhiều phần) và xác định chỗ trống còn lại trong từng phần của tấm vật liệu. - Chọn phần có không gian trống phù hợp nhất cho vật phẩm tiếp theo sao cho không gian trống còn lại sau khi cắt là nhỏ nhất, tức là phần còn lại gần như đầy. - Cắt vật phẩm vào tấm vật liệu: Nếu không có phần không gian nào vừa, tạo một tấm vật liệu mới và cắt vật phẩm vào đó. - Lặp lại cho đến khi tất cả các vật phẩm được cắt xong. ## 3. Kanapsack algorithm Knapsack sử dụng phương pháp dynamic programming. Bài toán knapsack là một bài toán lập trình tuyến tính với một ràng buộc. Bài toán knapsack được sử dụng để tìm ra giải pháp tốt nhất cho tất cả các vật phẩm có thể được đóng gói vào túi. Vì lý do này, phương pháp lập trình động (dynamic programming) được sử dụng trong việc giải bài toán knapsack. Lập trình động xác định giải pháp tối ưu của một bài toán đa biến bằng cách phân tách nó thành nhiều giai đoạn, mỗi giai đoạn là một bài toán con với một biến đơn. ## Test Results | **Policy** | **Average Trim Loss and Respective Filled Ratio** | |------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------| | **Greedy (GreedyPolicy)** | Filled ratio: 0.206

author: acelaya
body:
Part of #2124 

Change logic to determine if the GeoLite2 db file needs to be downloaded, in an attempt to address recurrent issues where people report they are hitting GeoLite's download API limits.

Current approach has two main problems:

1. The condition to perform the download is based on the existing GeoLite db file metadata, which includes the time in which it was built. If it's older than 35 days, Shlink tries to download it.
    This has presented problems in the past, due to stateful services which continue referencing an old version of the metadata, and database builds released with incorrect metadata, which make Shlink think they are outdated.
2. There's no historical information of previous downloads, which means Shlink could retry and fail indefinitely in case of an error.

This PR introduces a new table in the database where Shlink tracks download attempts, and their results (success or error).

Using this, Shlink can avoid subsequent attempts if there has been a number of consecutive download errors, making sure there's no more than a small number of attempts per day.

Additionally, it can use this to also know when was the last successful attempt, and download again after a reasonable number of days.

The exact rules of the algorithm introduced here are:

1. Get the last 15 download attempts.
2. If the max amount of consecutive errors has been reached (15), skip the download if the last one is less than 2 days old.
3. If there are no attempts at all or the database file itself does not exist, try to download the database.
4. If the last attempt is an error but we haven't reached the max amount of errors, try to download the database.
5. If the last attempt was successful and is older than 30 days, try to download the database.

### Todo

- [x] Test performance as the table grows (`EXPLAIN` in MySQL shows the index on `date_updated` may not be used when ordering the result. Maybe `id` needs to be used instead).
    EDIT: The index is in fact being used and making it very efficient. With 2M rows, sorting by `date_updated` (which is indexed) takes 0.001s, while sorting by `date_created` (which is NOT indexed) takes more than 3s.
- [x] Wrap process in transaction and lock using the database rather than a symfony locker.
    EDIT: I tried to lock via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and a database transaction, but didn't result in properly locked rows. I need to investigate further but I'll keep the filesystem lock for now.
- [x] Verify the mechanism to resolve the filesystem ID is working as expected and resolves different values for, eg. docker containers.
- [x] Log reason for which a database download was triggered:
    - No download attempts exist.
    - The database file does not exist.
    - Last attempt was error but no max consecutive errors were reached.
    - Last attempt was successful but it's older than 30 days.

author: daxpedda
body:
This bumps `stdarch` to https://github.com/rust-lang/stdarch/commit/684de0d6fef708cae08214fef9643dd9ec7296e1 to get in https://github.com/rust-lang/stdarch/pull/1677 (tracked in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133908).

From the [commit history](https://github.com/rust-lang/stdarch/compare/e5e00aab0a8c8fa35fb7865e88fa82366f615c53...684de0d6fef708cae08214fef9643dd9ec7296e1) I deduced that there shouldn't be any changes to Rust necessary.

From past PRs I'm assuming that bumping `stdarch` like this is fine, but please let me know if this is somehow inappropriate or requires something more to be done!

author: cebarobot
body:
Previously, the global instruction counter variable (g_nr_guest_instr) would be reset to 1 when executing nemu_trap 0x101 (start profiling) or receiving ctrl-c signal to start checkpointing, so that profiling and profiling mechanism could create checkpoints in specified intervals.

However, g_nr_guest_instr is a very important variable, which are and will be used in CSRs (minstret, mtime, mcycle) and timer device (clint). It's not good to reset it during running.

This patch modifies the original reset_inst_counters(): it now records current instr count as base with get_abs_instr_count(), and rename the function to start_profiling(). per_bb_profile() is also modified to use the difference between origin count and base as new instr count.

author: gwolf-011235
body:
### Overview

1. Adds integration tests with pytest
2. Adds macro for conditional code removal of DEBUG messages
3. Update coverage gutter search path

### 1. Adds integration tests with pytest

Pytest is an easy to use test framework written in Python [[LINK](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/)]. 
In combination with the libraray requests [[LINK](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)] we can easliy write tests to check behavior of our server.

#### dev container update
Pytest and requests exist as debian package. These are not the newest versions but they'll do. The packages can be easily added. Dev container needs to be rebuild.

#### test directory layout

A new subdirectory `integration` houses all python tests. Right now there are two "packages" as subdirectories server_response and server_management. This separation was necessary because of the test structure: 
 - server_response uses a single server instance to send requests to 
  - server_management is for starting and stopping server instances (right now only signals test)

The src files for unittest have been moved to subdirectory /unit. This means this PR has many files changed, but they were only moved

#### test_files

I added some example tests. Some are commented out because they don't work right now (e.g. POST, which is fixed via #108 ). Many more can be added. 
Some notes (see docs of pytest for more details):
- Each file is a module as is denoted by test_* (this is what pytest searches for)
- Each test function starts with test_* (again for pytest)
- There are conftest.py files which can configure test environment. Main use is for test fixtures of pytest. Right now we have one fixture which starts a server instance and keeps it running. Since this is defined in the file of server_response package it is not used in server_management

#### Coverage
We can also start kcov in front of the server to capture coverage. In this mode the tests take longer, because of longer startup

#### Makefile
There are new targets:
- make test2: runs integration tests
- make coverage2: runs integration tests with coverage

### 2. Adds macro for conditional code removal of DEBUG messages

Apart from increasing the loglevel, we can now remove the debug messages entirely, instead of just silencing them. If the macro DEBUG_MSG is not defined the macro LOG_DEBUG is replaced with `if (0) std::err`. Since this code does nothing (it is always false) it should be removed by the compiler, increasing our speed (since we don't even send the debug msg).
The macro is activated by default in Makefile, but can be deactivated by setting variable NODEBUG=1 

### 3. Update coverage gutter search path

Coverage gutter search path now searches for `.vscode/coverage/*`. This way it also looks in subdirectory to find cov.xml. Beforehand we created cov.xml in .vscode/coverage/ with running coverage two times. I found out that kcov produces cov.xml output anyway, but stores it in subdirectory. So now coverage gutters work without this extra step. Updated target coverage accordingly.

**Policy id = 1:**
_**Thuật toán sinh cột (Column Generation)**_
1. **Khởi tạo mẫu cắt:**
Trong hàm get_action, thuật toán bắt đầu với chi phí tối thiểu ban đầu là vô cực (min_cost = float("inf")) và lặp qua các mẫu cắt tiềm năng.
2. **Tạo mẫu cắt mới:**
Hàm _generate_cutting_pattern được sử dụng để tạo một mẫu cắt mới. Thuật toán duyệt qua các product và các stock, sắp xếp product theo kích thước lớn dần, tìm vị trí khả dụng và tính toán trim_loss để đánh giá hiệu quả của mẫu cắt.
3. **Cập nhật và kết thúc:**
Nếu mẫu cắt mới giảm được chi phí (trim_loss nhỏ hơn), thuật toán cập nhật mẫu cắt tốt nhất vào danh sách pattern. Quá trình lặp sẽ dừng khi không tìm được mẫu mới hoặc chi phí không còn được cải thiện. Action tốt nhất sẽ được trả về dựa trên mẫu cắt tối ưu đã tìm được.

**Policy Id  = 2:**
**_Thuật toán Greedy:_**
1. **Sắp xếp sản phẩm theo diện tích giảm dần:**
Trong hàm_generate_columns, các sản phẩm được sắp xếp theo diện tích giảm dần (sorted_products). 
2. **Chọn vị trí cắt tốt nhất:**
Trong vòng lặp tìm vị trí cắt (_find_valid_position), thuật toán duyệt qua tất cả các vị trí có thể đặt sản phẩm trên kho (stock) và chọn vị trí đầu tiên phù hợp để đặt sản phẩm. 
3. **Chọn mẫu cắt tốt nhất:**
Trong hàm get_action, thuật toán duyệt qua các mẫu cắt (cut_patterns) và chọn mẫu cắt đầu tiên hoặc tốt nhất theo tiêu chí đơn giản (diện tích còn thừa nhỏ nhất).

author: hanneswell
body:
Since Java-12 users can configure a JVM to disallow the installation of a SecurityManager at runtime. The default value of the configuration has changed over the following versions and since Java-24 it's finally not possible anymore under any circumstances to install a SecurityManager at runtime (see [JEP-486](https://openjdk.org/jeps/486)).

To quote from [JEP-411](https://openjdk.org/jeps/411):
```
Since Java 12, the end user has been able to prevent [dynamic installations of a Security Manager] by setting
the system property java.security.manager to disallow on the command line (java -Djava.security.manager=disallow ...)
-- this causes System::setSecurityManager to throw an UnsupportedOperationException. Starting in Java 18,
the default value of java.security.manager will be disallow[...].`
```
To determine if setting a SecurityManager is allowed, it's therefore not sufficient to just check the version of the running JVM, if it's a VM for Java-12 up to 23 (including). In case of the latter it has to be tested explicitly if setting a SecurityManager is supported.

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of changes to add and manage course resources in the application. The changes include new controllers, request interfaces, middleware validations, schema definitions, route configurations, and service methods. Below are the most important changes grouped by their themes:

### Controllers and Request Interfaces:

* Added `getAllCourseResourceController`, `addCourseResourceController`, `updateCourseResourceController`, and `deleteCourseResourceController` to handle course resource operations in `src/controllers/course.resources.controllers.ts`.
* Introduced request interfaces `VerifiedCourseRequest`, `VerifiedCourseRecourseRequest`, `AddCourseResourceRequestBody`, and `UpdateCourseResourceRequestBody` in `src/controllers/request/course.resource.request.ts`.

### Middleware Validations:

* Added `existingCourseValidation`, `courseResourceValidation`, `existingCourseResourceValidation`, and `existingResourceTypeValidation` middleware for validating course and resource data in `src/middlewares/course.resources.middlewares.ts`.

### Schema Definitions:

* Defined various resource schemas including `DocumentResourceInfo`, `LinkResourceInfo`, `AssignmentResourceInfo`, and `AnnouncementResourceInfo` along with the `CourseResource` schema in `src/models/schemas/course.resource.schema.ts`.

### Routes Configuration:

* Configured new routes for managing course resources, including adding, updating, and deleting resources in `src/routes/course.resources.routes.ts`.
* Updated `courses.routes.ts` to include the new resource routes under the course routes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed68620a0a06ba96140591999436bbd530eb184a41cb54042d2c390f7f17d0a8R27-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ed68620a0a06ba96140591999436bbd530eb184a41cb54042d2c390f7f17d0a8R53-R55)

### Service Methods:

* Implemented `getCourseResources`, `addCourceResources`, `updateCourseResource`, and `deleteCourseResource` methods in `src/services/course.resources.services.ts` to handle database operations for course resources.
* Added `courseResources` collection to the `DatabaseService` in `src/services/database.services.ts`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21edf10914af79583a88f49c52ca0eb94e8087752bcc9c546768a76c86136f8bR8-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21edf10914af79583a88f49c52ca0eb94e8087752bcc9c546768a76c86136f8bL36-R60)

### Utility Functions:

* Introduced `simpleControlWrapper` utility function in `src/utils/handler.ts` to simplify controller function handling.

Hier mein erster Wurf für eine Restrukturierung von `plugins.md`. Dabei liegt der Fokus auf der Kapitelstruktur, es sind noch einige Gaps offen:

- [x] Beispiele
- [x] Tabellen mit allen Werten

Out-of-scope in diesem PR:

- [ ] Englische Version

- Beschreibung der einzelnen Plugins
- Detailierte Beschreibung von Pipelines

Beim Review koennt ihr gerne direkt korrigieren und auf den Branch pushen, er ist offen für Maintainers (vielleicht bei groesseren Aenderung noch einen Review Kommentar).

<details>
<summary>Random Opinion following ..., nicht wichtig :-)</summary>
Darueberhinaus habe ich noch ein paar kleine Anmerkungen (sorry, ich kann nicht anders :-), die aber für den PR nicht relevant sind:

* "Plugin" ist eine etwas unglueckliche Bezeichnung, das sie in vielen anderen Faellen, _externen_ code und Konventionen bezeichnen, die ausserhalb des Kernprojekts leben und vorgegebene APIs implementieren. Im Falle von evcc ist aber die Liste der Plugins fix und koennen nicht selbst ergaenzt werden. Z.b. muesste man für eine Resol VBus Integrationen den core-code erweitern. In meinen Augen handelt es sich vielmehr um _Integrationen_, bei der externe _Sources_ (oder _Producer_) und _Sinks_ (oder _Consumer_) eingebunden werden, so wie sie z.b. in dem klassischen [EAI Patterns](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/) Buch beschrieben sind. Mir ist klar das im Kontext von evcc "Integrationen" anders interpretiert wird (i.e. wie man evcc *in* andere Systeme integrieren kann, also mehr eine "API" Beschreibung), daher sollten man es auch so lassen. Ich will hier _keine_ Diskussion starten, sondern mein innerer Spiesser wollte das einfach loswerden :-P und evtl. hilft das in Diskussionen um Missverstaendnisse zu vermeiden.

* Das "combined status" plugin passt in meinen Augen nicht wirklich in die Liste, da es nicht für alle Geraete genutzt werden kann (für `meter` macht das keinen Sinn, oder ?). Vielmehr wuerde ich es als Eigenschaft von `vehicle` sehen, bei denen Plugins genutzt werden koenne. Your mileage may vary.
</details>

**Idea**

Place a background composable behind the title content that handles all windows draggable header related stuff. This way, everything inside the title bar is placed **on top** of the composable that forwards the events to the draggable header.

**Issues this solves**

when clicking a dropdown menu in the title bar, the popup did not pop up until the next mouse move => fixed

**TODO**

* I added a `Box` around the title content, apply the modifier to it instead of the title bar composable and place the title bar composable inside the box with a simple `fillMaxSize` Modifier - I'm pretty sure it does not change anything, still, it needs to be tested on mac and linux as well once
* the macos implementation does use `customTitleBarMouseEventHandler` as well - it may be necessary to use the same fix there? I don't know, I don't have a mac and I don't know if the mac has the same issues
* for the sake of minimal adjustments I kept the `customTitleBarMouseEventHandler` as is (also because I don't know how it is used on mac) - it may be possible to simplifiy it like following as there is no need to try to detect if we are over a user control or not anymore because of the layerig of the background composable and the content.

```
internal fun Modifier.customTitleBarMouseEventHandler(titleBar: CustomTitleBar): Modifier =
    pointerInput(Unit) {
        val currentContext = currentCoroutineContext()
        awaitPointerEventScope {
            while (currentContext.isActive) {
                awaitPointerEvent(PointerEventPass.Main)
                titleBar.forceHitTest(false)
            }
        }
    }
```

Fix #424

author: som-sm
body:
Currently, when the second argument to `Set-Optional` is `any`, it returns an index signature. And this because `Set-Optional` uses `Pick`. ```ts type T = SetOptional<{a: 1; b: 2}, any>; // => type T = {[x: string]: any} ``` This PR modifies this behaviour to instead return all keys marked as optional. ```ts type T = SetOptional<{a: 1; b: 2}, any>; // => type T = {a?: 1; b?: 2} ``` Similar changes made for `Set-Required` & `Set-Readonly`.
Additionally, also fixes `Set-Optional` when instantiated with unions.

body:
Adding draft parameter option to create pull request.
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-a-pull-request

At Airflow, we effectively use the cherry-picker tool to backport changes, which has been highly beneficial in saving maintainers' time.

Currently, we have configured cherry-picker in our workflows, utilizing the GITHUB_TOKEN to create backport PRs. However, our workflows are not triggered on these backported PRs. This limitation occurs because GitHub prevents recursive workflows when using the default token.

https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/triggering-a-workflow#triggering-a-workflow-from-a-workflow .

To address this, we would like to create backport PRs in draft state. maintainer can then change them to the "Ready for Review" state, which will subsequently trigger the workflows.

Thank you @potiuk for the suggestion this.

author: leonvanbokhorst
body:
Implement a three-layer cognitive architecture (NOVA) using Ollama LLM integration:

- Add Reactive Layer (≤10 words responses)
  * Fast, instinctive responses with temperature 0.3
  * Strict word limit and imperative form
  * Limited response length (num_predict: 50)

- Add Responsive Layer (context-aware)
  * Maintains context history of last 5 messages
  * Balanced temperature (0.7)
  * Medium-length responses (num_predict: 100)

- Add Reflective Layer (pattern analysis)
  * Deep thinking with pattern recognition
  * Higher temperature (0.7) for creative insights
  * Maintains history of learned patterns

Features:
- Parallel processing using asyncio
- Clear terminal output with emojis and formatting
- Configurable model selection via MODEL_NAME constant
- Error handling and resource cleanup
- Kafka integration for message distribution

Example demonstrates anxiety management scenario through
different cognitive processing depths.

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement a three-layer cognitive architecture (NOVA) using Ollama LLM, featuring Reactive, Responsive, and Reflective layers for varied processing depths. Integrate Kafka for message distribution and use asyncio for parallel processing. Enhance user interaction with formatted terminal output and ensure robust operation with error handling and resource cleanup. Deploy using Docker containers for Kafka and Zookeeper.

New Features:
- Introduce a three-layer cognitive architecture (NOVA) using Ollama LLM integration, consisting of Reactive, Responsive, and Reflective layers for different processing depths and temporal scales.
- Implement parallel processing using asyncio to enhance performance across the three cognitive layers.
- Add Kafka integration for message distribution, enabling efficient communication between different layers.

Enhancements:
- Provide clear terminal output with emojis and formatting for better user interaction.
- Enable configurable model selection via a MODEL_NAME constant, allowing flexibility in model usage.
- Implement error handling and resource cleanup to ensure robust operation.

Deployment:
- Set up Docker containers for Kafka and Zookeeper to facilitate the deployment of the messaging infrastructure.

## Detailed description

As ARMv8-A changed entirely debug interactions, a new target was needed.

This implements a new basic target for ARMv8-A that only support AArch64 for now.

I tested all those changes with a [Solitude AML-S905D3-CC](https://libre.computer/products/aml-s905d3-cc/) on core 0 in u-boot (JTAG access can be enabled with `smc 0x82000040 2`)

Things left as todo that will not be tackled by this PR:
- Float registers
- AArch32 support (Lot of cortexar.c could be reused for this)
- Any relevant ARMv8-A extensions to expose (Pointer Authentication)
- Possibly weird CoreSight tables where the CTI component isn't after the DC

author: martinloeper
body:
. I noticed that `update_dependencies` was not interpreted correctly in the `Helm | Dependency` steps if condition.
It looks like the correct way to evaluate the condition is to wrap it with `${{ }}`.

see discussion in: https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/1173

see also: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#jobsjob_idif

> When you use expressions in an if conditional, you can, optionally, omit the ${{ }} expression syntax because GitHub Actions automatically evaluates the if conditional as an expression. However, this exception does not apply everywhere.

author: borewit
body:
Add support for LZ4 file format, which is an archive created by one of a variety of LZ4 compression utilities.

On a positive detection the following is returned:
- extension: `lz4`
- MIME-type: `application/x-lz4`, lacking formal MIME-type assignment

Related documentation:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LZ4_(compression_algorithm)
- https://fileinfo.com/extension/lz4

Resolves: sindresorhus/file-type#444

body:
### **MEMBERS CONTRIBUTION**

* Nguyen Tuan Phong - 2252612: Best Fit & First Fit Heuristic (BFFF Heuristic) (100%)
* Nguyen Thien Phuc - 2252645: Skyline Algorithm (100%)
* Truong Quang Nha - 2152822: Report & real case study (100%)

### **ALGORITHMS DESCRIPTION**

**Skyline Algorithm**
The Skyline algorithm is employed in solving the cutting stock problem, a classic optimization challenge in operations research. This problem involves cutting large stock materials, such as metal sheets, wood planks, or fabric rolls, into smaller pieces to meet specific size requirements while minimizing material waste. The Skyline algorithm is used to efficiently identify non-dominated cutting patterns based on criteria like material utilization, waste minimization, and production cost. By finding a "skyline" of optimal patterns, the algorithm helps narrow down choices and facilitates more efficient decision-making.

**Best Fit & First Fit Heuristic**
The Best Fit First Fit (BFFF) heuristic is a hybrid approach that combines elements of both the First Fit and Best Fit heuristics to solve the cutting stock problem. In this method, the algorithm first attempts to place each item into the least leftover space (Best Fit). If this doesn’t result in an efficient solution, it then re-evaluates and places the item into the first new stock (First Fit). This combination aims to leverage the simplicity and speed of First Fit, while also improving material utilization by incorporating the efficiency of Best Fit.

### **Results:**
After running 30 rounds, these are average results for 4 policies:
| Policy | Average Filled Ratio | Average Trim Loss | Average Execution Time (seconds) |
|:---------:|:--------:|:---------:|:---------:|
| Greedy Algorithm    | 0,18 | 0,20 | 31,36 |
| Random Algorithm    | 0,69 | 0,78 | 0,25 |
| Skyline Algorithm    | 0,102 | 0,31 | 18,86 |
| BFFF Heuristic    | 0,106 | 0,18 | 48,75 |

body:
<!-- Your title above should be a short description of what
was changed. Do not include the issue number in the title. -->

#### References to other Issues or PRs
<!-- If this pull request fixes an issue, write "Fixes #NNNN" in that exact
format, e.g. "Fixes #1234" (see
https://tinyurl.com/auto-closing for more information). Also, please
write a comment on that issue linking back to this pull request once it is
open. -->

Includes the changes from gh-27369.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

Adds type annotations to all methods of MatrixBase which is the superclass of Matrix, ImmutableMatrix etc. This also requires adding some annotations to other code that either is used by MatrixBase or that has type annotations and uses Matrix.

In the particular case of MatrixBase the type situation is copmlicated by the fact that there are many different subclasses and there is a need to keep track of whether or not a method defined on MatrixBase or a function that operates with MatrixBase returns e.g. mutable vs immutable or dense vs sparse matrices. I think I have managed to make this understood by a type checker and have fixed a few bugs where the types used and returned are inconsistent.

Another complicate in the matrices code is that there are a number of methods that are overloaded and that return e.g. different types depending on some parameter like `M.rref(pivots=True)`. These things require the use of `@overload` for a type checker to understand what the types are. In general it is much nicer if functions only ever return one well defined type. Having multiple argument signatures is also problematic for type checking but much less so than having multiple return types.

#### Other comments

I am putting this here firstly to show what it would look like to add type annotations for all methods of a class like MatrixBase so that we can discuss exactly how we want to apply type annotations. I would also encourage people to ask questions about why I have used particular annotations in particular places and what the differences are. If we are to apply annotations like this throughout the codebase then it will be necessary for sympy maintainers and contributors to have some understanding of what the annotations means and how to use them. It has taken me some considerable time to gain enough of an understanding that I can write the annotations that are here in this PR.

There are a number of choices to be made like how exactly to use `type: ignore`, how specific the annotations need to be etc. For `type: ignore` there different cases for why I have used it:

- In some cases it is because of limitations in the type checkers (often bugs in mypy).
- In some cases the code in sympy is actually buggy and should be fixed. For now though when adding annotations it is better just to mark it as ignored and the `type: ignore` serves as a reminder that probably the code needs to be improved.
- In other cases the code is correct but the use of a type checker means that it would need to be written more simply so that a type checker could understand what is happening. I would consider it still worthwhile to change that code but for now it is better to use `type: ignore`.

There are also cases where the signatures can be simplified a lot by just using e.g. `**kwargs: Any` but then that hides what the optional arguments are from both type checkers and from users. In some cases here I have used `**kwargs: Any` and in others I have expanded that to list exactly what all of the arguments and types are. Using `Any` can be a prudent shortcut when adding annotations to a large codebase but it also prevents those particular annotations from doing anything useful.

There are also choices like what type aliases to use e.g. here I have used `SBasic = Basic | complex` as a way of meaning "`Basic` or sympifiable". Ideally we would centralise these type aliases somewhere and make them available for downstream code to use as well.

There are also questions about how to make the docs work. There seem to be bugs/issues with using autotools in combination with type annotations that result in sphinx needing to know somehow about different classes or type aliases. I am not sure what is a good general strategy for that.

Lastly I would not propose that we rush to add annotations everywhere throughout the whole codebase. I do think though that certain key types like `Matrix`, `Poly`, `Expr`, etc should be fully annotated. This PR shows what that could look like for the most complicated class (having an absurd number of methods).

author: u413-284-si
body:
## Overview
1. Add DeleteHandler class
2. Add deleteFile() and deleteDirectory() to FileSystemPolicy
3. Add DirectoryGuard subclass to FileSystemPolicy
4. Integrate MethodDelete into ResponseBodyHandler, Server
5. Fix Content-Type recognition: json
6. Add unittests

### re 1.
- New DeleteHandler to manage DELETE requests
- basically same structure as AutoIndexHandler and FileWriteHandler
- differentiates between several cases: 
1. files
2. directories
3. nonExistent resource (sets status code 404)
4. permission denied (sets status code 403)
5. any other error (sets status code 500)
- returns string containing json body on success, nothing in error case

### re 2.
- deleteFile() uses remove to delete files, throws on error
- deleteDirectory() works recursively to be able to delete non-empty directories, it will traverse the whole directory tree and delete all files and directories in a bottom-to-top approach and finally delete the empty target directory
- in case of errors the throw will be caught in the DeleteHandler

### re 3.
- due to the possibility of a throw while traversing the directory structure, a "guard" for the DIR* pointer was required
- to open a directory a DIR* pointer is created and needs to be closed when done in order to have no leaks
- w/o the guard a throw would leave (potentially multiple) pointers open
- the guard serves to close the pointer upon leaving its scope by utilising its dtor to call closedir
- the guard is implemented as nested subclass in FileSystemPolicy as this is the only class to require it

### re 4.
- MethodDelete is being handled in the ResponseBodyHandler
- check added to allow for directories to be deleted even if they don't have an autoindex, similar to the check allowing for non-exisiting files to be created by POST requests

### re 5.
- the response bodies of POST and DELETE requests are formatted in json
- added check in appendHeaders() to assign Content-Type: application/json in that case

### re 6.
- unittests to test all cases of DeleteHandler
- additional request reqDel to test manually (of in future with pytest)

closes #80

author: larshelge
body:
In event and enrollment analytics table statements, we have 64 lines of SQL code to produce two fields - `createdbydisplayname` and `lastupdatedbydisplayname`. IMHO this is too much complexity and code to produce two fields. It is hard to reason about, makes the update slower, and makes it hard to port to Doris/ClickHouse. 

I have been doing some research on event/tracker DHIS 2 instances, and I could see that typically either `createdbyuserinfo` is not set at all, or is fully set with all properties (first name, username, username). I have not seen a partial value yet. If some implementations have a partial `userinfo` object for enrollments/events, we should fix that once with a SQL statement, and/or fix the issue with tracker that causes this in the first place. That is better than "fixing" it every time analytics table update runs.

author: paul-maidment
body:
When a new node is added to a Day 2 cluster via a BMH, the resulting BMH is copied to the spoke cluster. Presently, the spoke cluster will always show this with a status of 'poweredOn: false' when the BMH should have a status of 'poweredOn: true'.

This PR changes that by forcing a status update in the `ensureSpokeBMH` As the SpokeBMH is not managed (or even reconciled in any way) by Metal3 then it is acceptable for us to manage the status when copying the BMH to the node.

author: greglucas
body:
This builds on the packet refactor work (the final commit of this PR is relevant to continuation packets) and adds continuation packet support to the XTCE parsing and packet generation. This adds logic to concatenate packet data fields together across successive packets (if there was too much data to fit in a single CCSDS packet or it was logically better to split by other teams).
- Add warnings if packets are out of sequence within a given apid.
- Add ability to remove secondary header bytes from subsequent packets.
  ``definition.packet_generator(data, combine_segmented_packets=True, secondary_header_bytes=4)``

Notes:
- This is only in the XTCE packet parsing definition generator for now, so thoughts on doing this up a level are welcome. I chose not to to keep it as "raw" as possible at that stage, but could see an argument either way.
- I've chosen to keep old behavior with `combine_segmented_packets=False`, so this is opt-in behavior. I'm not sure if that is what we should do or if we should start combining them right away and have it be opt-out instead?

closes #114

author: bobjacobsen
body:
Now that production release 5.10 has been tagged v5.10 and released, we need to merge that branch (which also contained 5.9.8) back into master.  

That way, if somebody someday starts a branch from tag v5.10, it will be in the direct line from master and won't have the version control files show as changes, which in turn will revert them when that new branch is merged.  

This should be merged before the branch for release 5.11.1 is created to keep the version information in the right sequence on master.

This pull request introduces several changes to the parser, lexer, and resolver components of the codebase. The most significant changes include adding support for the `int` keyword, refactoring the AST structure, and improving the variable scoping mechanism.

### Lexer and Token Updates:
* Added support for the `int` keyword in the lexer and token definitions. (`src/lexer/mod.rs`, `src/lexer/token.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-38925686e9d8d144d9f852e93c0cafe472f340651a5ffbbdd705c0f80265987cR54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d417470a8403d56521df4a86a0be785c8970dac490fc17e1a06f8da43ea32d91R59)

### Parser Refactoring:
* Refactored `FunctionDef` to use a `Block` instead of `Vec<BlockItem>` for the function body. (`src/parser/ast.rs`)
* Updated various parser methods to handle the new `Block` structure, including `function_def`, `block_item`, `statement`, and `compound`. (`src/parser/mod.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fc6a8d66b8cb6bd48a119a70e489cbcef82e7f551e7cf08e8e972ef4e774ef49L215-R242) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fc6a8d66b8cb6bd48a119a70e489cbcef82e7f551e7cf08e8e972ef4e774ef49L456-R484) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fc6a8d66b8cb6bd48a119a70e489cbcef82e7f551e7cf08e8e972ef4e774ef49R493-R526) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fc6a8d66b8cb6bd48a119a70e489cbcef82e7f551e7cf08e8e972ef4e774ef49L510-R545)
* Introduced a new error type `InvalidDeclaration` for invalid declarations in specific contexts. (`src/parser/mod.rs`)

### AST and Visitor Changes:
* Added support for visiting compound statements in the AST visitors. (`src/parser/ast.rs`, `src/parser/stmt.rs`, `src/parser/pretty_print_ast.rs`, `src/tacky.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b78363c945458ba512de20a9df6c5b2536b373fd115e181701f89ee0e7acf6d3R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b78363c945458ba512de20a9df6c5b2536b373fd115e181701f89ee0e7acf6d3R115) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-be9592c5274e99eabeeab97e32d7bf873e5360023df6f66946a0656525eab5f8R16-R21) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d9d8baaf7bad9777aceb7650afc6ef7c4507b8ab59f4135b883cac8b4f9e4aadR127-R144) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-80431fc27e6e28bbf208b6d06537efd75c1b6e4bbe4e6b50039e6a3aa8e94864R242-R245)

### Resolver Enhancements:
* Refactored the resolver to use a scoped variable map for better handling of variable scoping. (`src/resolver/mod.rs`, `src/resolver/scoped_var_map.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8011e2789b524940bae5b965595c4bd762e81f29f35ded30f1afd12e38d6d233R1-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8011e2789b524940bae5b965595c4bd762e81f29f35ded30f1afd12e38d6d233R26-R37) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8011e2789b524940bae5b965595c4bd762e81f29f35ded30f1afd12e38d6d233L89-R94)

These changes collectively improve the parser's handling of new keywords, enhance the structure of the AST, and provide a more robust mechanism for variable scoping.

2.Brief Description
BestFit:The Best-Fit Bin Packing heuristic can be adapted for use in the Cutting Stock Problem
(CSP), though the two problems have different structures. While CSP involves cutting
larger stock pieces into smaller pieces to meet demands, the Best-Fit algorithm focuses on
fitting items into bins with minimal unused space. However, the goal in both problems is
to minimize waste or unused material.
Step 1:Define Cutting Patterns
Step 2: Sort Cutting Patterns by Efficiency
Step 3: Place Items (Demand)
Step 4: Repeat until Demand is Met
Step 5: Adjust Stock Usage

ordered according to nonincreasing sizes. Put the next element from L as low and as
much to the left as possible.
Step 1:Initialization
Step 2: Placement of Pieces
Step 3: Update the Available Space
Step 4: Repeat Until All Pieces Are Placed

**1. Introduction:**
In this pull request is the implementation of 2 algorithms: Bottom Left Decreasing and Next Fit Decreasing Height.

**Brief Description:**

**Bottom-Left-Decreasing (BLD) Algorithm:** The algorithm places items in a stock by sorting them in descending size order and fitting them from the bottom-left corner. The algorithm only make use of original orientations to minimize unused space.

**Next-Fit-Decreasing-Height (NFDH) Algorithm:** The NFDH algorithm sorts items by height and places them row by row in a stock. If an item doesn't fit in the current row, it starts a new one, also checking both orientations to optimize space usage.

# Group 141's Submission - Math Modeling Assignment - Semester 241

## Group Members
<!-- Describe cutting stock problem -->
* Nguyễn Phú Thịnh - 2313293
* Đặng Huyền Vũ - 2313950
* Phạm Xuân Bắc - 2310280

## Assignment: Algorithm for Cutting Stock Problem
This pull request introduces the implementation and comparison of two algorithms for solving the **Two-Dimensional Cutting Stock Problem (2D-CSP)**, a critical optimization challenge in manufacturing and logistics. The goal is to minimize material waste while fulfilling specific cutting demands efficiently.

## Algorithms
This implementation features 2 policies aiming to solve the 2D cutting stock problem: the Strip-Packing Algorithm and the Heuristic-Greedy Algorithm. The policy seeks to minimize trim loss by considering product orientations and stock utilization.

### Strip-Packing Algorithm (policy_id = 1)
Strip-Packing Algorithm is an algorithm to prioritize placing along parallel edges. With its most notable pattern is a staircase within the first few steps taken in filling a stock.

### Heuristic-Greedy Algorithm (policy_id = 2)
This algorithm is a hybrid algorithm which is a combination of heuristic and greedy. Design for solving 2D-CSP for faster time executed and higher performance.  Focus on reducing as much waste in the first few products as possible ignoring potential long-term waste in the last stock due to not having enough product for filling. This particular method is effective with a moderate level of speed, although sensitive to cases where there's a lack of variety of products or when products' sizes are too small

## Features
* **Stock Optimization:** Minimizes material waste by optimizing cutting patterns.
* **Algorithm Comparison:** Includes performance analysis of Strip-Packing and Heuristic-Greedy algorithms on trim loss and filled ratio.
* **Scalable Framework:** Supports varying product dimensions and stock sizes.

## Result
| Metrics | Strip-Packing | Heuristic-Greedy |
| ------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| Filled Ratio | 0.18950 | 21.59030  |
| % Trim loss | 0.12580 | 15.80482 |
| Runtime | Slower | Faster |

### Key insights:
* The Strip-Packing algorithm is suitable for high-accuracy needs but slower in execution.
* The Heuristic-Greedy algorithm provides faster runtime and better trim loss reduction, nevertheles it's not stability and only use for a certain test case.

* **Library:** NumPy, gymnasium, Scipy

body:
## Implemented Algorithm ##
### Column Generation Algorithm (CG): ### 

This is an efficient algorithm for solving large Linear Programming (IP) problems with many variables and high complexity, which are difficult to solve using the traditional simplex method. In the 2DCSP problem, by relaxing the integer constraint, the Integer Linear Programming (ILP) problem is transformed into a standard IP problem that can be solved using the CG method.

The idea behind this approach is to focus on the basic variables at a given point in time, temporarily ignoring the non-basic variables. As non-basic variables have a value of 0 in an optimal solution, if a large proportion of variables are non-basic, the CG method can significantly reduce computational resources compared to the conventional simplex method.

### Genetic Algorithm (GA) : ###
The Genetic Algorithm generates an initial population (a solution to the problem) and expands it by creating neighboring solutions using operators such as addition, deletion, movement, and exchange. From this population, the best individuals are selected as the basis for mutation and crossover processes, which produce the next generations of solutions.

body:
### Genetic Algorithm Policy
**Description**: The policy is based on a genetic algorithm (GA) to evolve a population of potential solutions. Each individual (solution) is represented by a set of parameters (e.g., neural network weights), and the fitness is evaluated based on performance on a task (e.g., reinforcement learning problem). The best individuals are selected, crossed over, and mutated to form the next generation.

**Implementation**: 
1. Initialize a population with random solutions.
2. Evaluate the fitness of each solution.
3. Select the top-performing solutions (elitism or tournament selection).
4. Perform crossover and mutation on selected individuals to generate new solutions.
5. Repeat the evaluation and selection process over several generations.

**Results**: The genetic algorithm effectively evolved solutions that perform well on test data, with gradual improvements observed across generations.

---

### Actor-Critic Policy
**Description**: The Actor-Critic method combines two components: the actor (policy network) and the critic (value network). The actor selects actions based on the current state, while the critic evaluates the action by estimating the value function.

**Implementation**:
1. Initialize both the actor and critic networks.
2. The actor selects actions based on the policy, and the critic computes the value function.
3. Update the actor using the policy gradient and the critic using value-based updates (e.g., TD learning).

author: exploide
body:
This PR adds two commits.

1. Disable the browser's spell-checking on the download cradle code. This makes no sense, is ugly and distracted me multiple times. See also the screenshot in PowerHub's README which shows the ugly underlining from spell-checking. I recommend doing a new screenshot. :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye: 

2. I encountered a case where the stager could not connect to PowerHub due to a restrictive proxy. A call by `curl.exe` succeeded, which did not use any proxy. Ticking/unticking the "Use Web Proxy" checkbox did not make any difference. Apparently, the default behavior of `Net.WebClient` was already to use the proxy. This did only happen in the context of a newly created local administrator account. The PowerShell instance of a low-privileged AD user did not use the proxy. Anyway, I was in need to explicitly unset the web proxy. To make this easier, I added an option to the web proxy setting.

Not sure if you like it, since the setting is also possible via a small manual change and it turns the checkbox into a selection field. However, if you decide to not merge this, at least cherry-pick the first commit, because did I say it's ugly? :grin:

author: oshanrodrigo
body:
Datasets/ratings_with_splitted_bCategories.csv and Datasets/business.csv are the two dataset files currently in use for the ML model.

In an earlier commit, all the non-numeric values in the .csv dataset files were explicitly converted as strings or quoted to avoid the bug of creating invalid values (#NAME?) in the "business_id" column during data preprocessing activities. That commit has led to parsing the content in .csv dataset files incorrectly by the ML model.

With this commit, that issue has been resolved. Now the explicitly quoting process is applied only on the non-numeric values in .csv files that are used as INPUT for data preprocessing activites (e.g. yelp_academic_dataset_business.csv, ratings.csv).

Following are the reduced versions of the above dataset files:
    Datasets/Reduced_ratings_with_splitted_bCategories.csv
    Datasets/Reduced_business.csv

author: samuelallan72
body:
Since https://github.com/nushell/nushell/pull/14344 (4d3283e), the `++` (concat) operator does not support appending a bare value to a list.

The current nushell script will result in this error in latest nushell:

```
Error: nu::shell::type_mismatch

  × Type mismatch during operation.
    ╭─[mise.nu:14:47]
 13 │   let old_hooks = $old_config | get $field --ignore-errors | default []
 14 │   $env.config = ($old_config | upsert $field ($old_hooks ++ $new_hook))
    ·                                               ─────┬──── ─┬ ────┬────
    ·                                                    │      │     ╰── record<condition: closure, code: closure>
    ·                                                    │      ╰── type mismatch for operator
    ·                                                    ╰── list<closure>
 15 │ }
    ╰────
```

So here we can fix it, in a backwards compatible manner, by wrapping the `$new_hook` value in brackets
to form a list containing the single item.

author: theory
body:
Just before the release of Postgres 17, a [discussion] of the effect of DateStyle and TimeZone on datetime string formatting revealed that those effects violated the immutability of the jsonpath functions. Commit [cc4fdfa] fixed the issue by making the output of `.string()` on datetimes the same as normal JSON output: always according to the time zone with which a datetime was originally parsed, and always in ISO-8601 format.

Duplicate that change by removing the `ToString` method from the DateTime interface and all of its implementations, replacing it with `fmt.Stringer`, to always use `String`. Update the docs and tests in line with [cc4fdfa], as well. Remove the paragraph about DateStyle from the "Compatibility" section of the README, since it no longer impacts datetime formatting.

While at it, add `.util/pglist.go`, a utility to generate a list of `git diff` commands to run against the Postgres source when looking to sync changes in the future. Use it to then replicate additional changes between the previously-synced Postgres tag, `REL_17_BETA1` and the recently-released `REL_17_2`, including:

*   A note about the behavior of lax mode on array evaluation in the
    README.
*   Update number links to the Postgres source.
*   Add a few links to `jsonpath_exec.c` and `func.sgml` for
    `.util/pglist.go` to find, as it was not previously linked, so would
    not be in the list of files to diff.
*   Use `boolean` instead of `bool` in error messages, as updated in
    postgres/postgres@f2353dd.
*   Move `pg2go.pl` to `.util`.
*   Replace the `String() string` method in the `ast.Node` interface
    with `fmt.Stringer`

  [discussion]: https://postgr.es/m/5e8879d0-a3c8-4be2-950f-d83aa2af953a@eisentraut.org
  [cc4fdfa]: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/cc4fdfa
  [f2353dd]: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/f2353dd

author: dalathegreat
body:
### What
This PR makes the Atto 3 less likely to throw Events the first seconds on startup

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03354fb4-59e3-415f-a9d7-035e2150e387)

### Why
Feedback from flying tools video on the Atto 3, which reports CELL DEVIATION and UNDERVOLTAGE as soon as the battery starts.

### How
The issue was split into two parts
- Cell max/min values where updated async during OBD2 polling, causing the min to actually be larger than max for a few seconds. By adding ABS subtraction to compare the diff, we catch this edge case
- Pack undervoltage on startup. Due to the Datalayer having 370.0V as startup value, which is 10V lower than the Atto 3 minimum voltage (380.0V), we now init the value to 380.1V to avoid false positive events.

author: mkotowski
body:
## What was changed

Switch const key for SGR 21 to a more widely supported variant.

## Rationale

ECMA-48 and most common terminal emulators implement SGR 21 as double underline, which predates SGR 4 underline style extension. This behavior is much more common than "no bold" one.

Currently, `x/ansi` uses `[Nn]oBoldAttr` for SGR 21, but the consensus among terminal emulators (and ECMA-48) is to apply double underline or other visual indicator instead.

```sh
printf '\e[21mTest\e[m'
```

Double underline:

- **ECMA-48**
- WezTerm (flatpak 20240203-110809-5046fc22)
- KDE konsole 23.08.5
- Gnome Terminal Version 3.52.0 for GNOME 46 (Using VTE version 0.76.0 +BIDI +GNUTLS +ICU +SYSTEMD)

Single underline or other visual indicator:

- xterm (372)
- Linux console since Linux 4.17

Normal intensity / no bold:

- [Linux console before Linux 4.17](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man4/console_codes.4.html#:~:text=before%20Linux%204.17%2C%20this%20value%20set%20normal%20intensity)

## Impact

- This will break apps using the NoBold function, but `x` projects do not guarantee backwards compatibility.
- After a cursory search, `NoBold()` does not seem to be used (at least according to GitHub's search) and impact of the change should be minimal.
- This requires change in [charmbracelet/sequin](https://github.com/charmbracelet/sequin).

body:
## Change goal
Registrovanim korisnicima je dozvoljeno praćenje drugog naloga navigiranjem do stranice profila korisnika i aktiviranjem praćenja tog naloga. Takođe je dozvoljen prekid praćenja naloga. Objave korisnika koji su praćeni se pojavljuju na početnoj stranici korisnika, dok se praćenja mogu videti na stranici profila naloga koji su u vezi. Kako bi se aplikacija zaštitila od tzv. botova, potrebno je ograničiti broj praćenja koje korisnik može da izvrši u minutu. Korisnik može da zaprati proizvoljno mnogo
naloga, ali maksimalno 50 po minuti. Dodatno, potrebno je transakcijama rešiti konfliktnu situaciju pravilnog inkrementa broja pratilaca u slučaju ida više korisnika istovremeno zaprate isti nalog. U svrhu testiranja, dodati Thread.sleep() ili napisati jedinični test kojim bi se simulirao konkurentni pristup, poput primera sa vežbi.

## UI changes
Trenutno je ulogovan user koji se zove Novi i on prati Peru:
![1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a6d647f-daa3-4776-ab9d-8f226b90c2d9)
![2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6bed9aa-167b-402d-85c9-001c5d9f2890)

Novi otpraćuje Peru:
![3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dd7e5e8-ad1b-4051-ad08-cadbc6770b67)
![4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1af80bb9-4265-4652-8e00-98e4cb7bfc87)

Ovako izgleda kada se pristupi svom profilu (nema opcija za praćenje). Takođe, ovde se vidi i slučaj kada korisnik nema ni jednu objavu:
![5](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b59ff1fa-6d6f-4e11-a950-f55c1ac166d4)

author: exyi
body:
ko.observableArray would leak the original object to its 'arrayChanges' subscribers when instance method (such as 'push', 'splice') was used to modify the array. Knockout would pre-compute the diff passed to the subscribers before our validator was called.

* Knockout updated to b7b150a6 to remove an optimization which was the primary cause
* Made FakeObservableObject internal properties non-enumerable so make sure they don't propagate through coercer when assigned into an array.

body:
### **Descripcion**
**Se agregan las siguientes funcionalidades:**

**Selección de pais:** 
-Combo que permite una selección de un pais, cuando se elige, se generara un mapa centrándose en el pais elegido.

**Mapa interactivo:**
-Mapa dinámico, en el cual dada una lista de filtros para el mapa, el usuario podrá hacer clic en el lugar donde quiera ir y le aparecerán los intereses cercanos que selecciono en el combo. 

Con esto ya tenemos el pais, la latitud y longitud, la ciudad, calle y departamento.

**Notas:**

-Los iconos podremos cambiarlo por cualquiera que queramos. Si se quiere agregar un icono, es en la clase de MapIcons, en el cual recibe un map de los places, permitiéndonos definir una imagen para el tipo que le llegue.

-Se pueden agregar para que aparezcan mas puntos de interés. ya que esto lo hacemos utilizando la Api de Over Pass, en el cual dada una latitud y longitud, le podemos pasar una lista de resultados que queremos en forma de JSON.

Ejemplo: node["tourism"="museum"](around:6000, ${lat}, ${lng}); 

En esta consulta, con node le indicamos que estamos buscando nodos (que vendrían a ser los puntos de interés), con "tourism"="museum" especificamos buscar los nodos relacionados con el turismo, que en especifico sean museos.

Con el around estamos indicando que en un rango de 6000 metros, (a partir de las cords de lat y lng del marcador), nos muestre todos aquellos nodos en ese rango.

# Pull Request

## Description

This pull request includes changes to the `.github/actions/local/action.yml` and `main.go` files to enhance the functionality of the GitHub Action by adding a summary generation feature. The most important changes include updating the environment variable and adding a new function to generate the summary.

Enhancements to GitHub Action:

* [`.github/actions/local/action.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-ec968081d12d3c0f4a02a4bcbc5a1d95f7bd6797860ab4509c4dacec118f510fL9-R9): Updated the environment variable from `GITHUB_ACTION` to `RUNNING_IN_GITHUB_ACTION` to better reflect its purpose.

Code changes in `main.go`:

* [`main.go`](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261R4-R12): Added the `os` package import to handle environment variables.
* [`main.go`](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261R25-R39): Added the `GitHubActionSummary` function to generate a summary file when running in a GitHub Action environment. This function checks the `RUNNING_IN_GITHUB_ACTION` environment variable, writes a summary to the file specified by `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and logs the process.
* [`main.go`](diffhunk://#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261R4-R12): Updated the `main` function to call `GitHubActionSummary`, ensuring the summary generation is triggered when the program runs.

Fixes #117
